source: Independent read-only review of the exact revision-5 brief, spec, plan, test specification, graph, and Architect r5 APPROVE. Prior blocking C1-C6 decisions are checked for consistency; no product source or runtime behavior was changed.

findings.title: Pin recursive scalar and cardinality checks at the canonical fixture boundary
evidence: The r5 spec fixes scalar conventions and named fields for ImportProvenance, ImportLossEntry, ImportResult, the encrypted envelope, targets, plans, receipts, and errors.
Architect r5 marks the remaining per-variant scalar and empty-array precision gaps as medium advisories, not blocking contract gaps.
G008 and the test specification require every v2 variant plus both handshake success/error pairs in the canonical fixture.
findings.impact: A shallow parser test could accept an unexpected nested key or wrong empty-array cardinality while still passing the named fixture cases.
findings.recommendation: Make fixture/parser tests recursively closed and assert scalar type, constant, non-empty, and empty-array rules for every variant. This is an implementation proof strengthening, not a new path or API decision.

findings.title: Assert actual metadata-only result envelopes recursively
evidence: The r5 spec adds click_text, click_button_text, scroll_table, and drag to the shared gate and forbids value/valueBefore/valueAfter/ariaValue*/allRows and table-cell strings.
The test specification requires clean, unknown, and potentially-private coverage, with blocked states failing closed.
Architect r5 specifically advises checking real pageSnapshot/scroll result envelopes for value-bearing descendants, not only top-level keys.
findings.impact: A serializer could remove named top-level fields but leak a value through a nested snapshot, row, or action-result descendant.
findings.recommendation: Use recursive redaction assertions on the worker-visible envelopes and keep one negative per tool plus blocked-state assertions. No replanning is needed.

findings.title: Bind the eight proof keys to executable commands and durable evidence
evidence: The spec fixes padloc/.ch5/proof.yaml as authority and names the eight required command keys.
The graph and test specification require exact-SHA proof records, but the planning artifacts intentionally leave the command bodies and evidence directories to implementation.
findings.impact: A key could exist with a placeholder or non-consuming command and appear complete without proving the boundary.
findings.recommendation: When G008 lands, map each fixed key to an executable changed-only or cross-repository command and record its exact-SHA evidence path. The authority path and key names are already fixed, so this is not an ITERATE condition.

findings.title: Make the G003 to G005 background handoff mechanically visible
evidence: The plan and graph give G003 the passkey region, G005 the autofill region, and a serial dependency before G005 may edit background.ts.
The graph uses region-qualified background.ts ownership and the test specification requires a terminal handoff fixture, but it does not name a separate handoff artifact.
findings.impact: Reviewers could miss an accidental cross-region edit if the handoff is recorded only in prose.
findings.recommendation: Have G003 leave its existing terminal handoff fixture and have G005 verify the passkey-region exclusion before editing. Keep all new proof inside already-owned test/artifact paths; do not invent a public API.

findings.title: Make the synthetic artifact scanner cover every declared leak channel
evidence: G009 fixes the canonical padloc command, repository-local fixture directories, padloc-owned evidence directory, and non-zero-on-leak behavior.
The test specification names stdout, logs, argv, screenshots, artifacts, workflow state, temporary profiles, and queues as safety boundaries.
findings.impact: The runner could be green while scanning only a subset of the declared channels or leaving stale temporary state behind.
findings.recommendation: Require the scanner to recurse through every listed channel, fail on raw-value markers or unsafe keys, and verify temporary profile/queue cleanup. The runner, paths, and fake-data posture are already fixed.

positiveEvidence: The brief maps all ten required outcomes to the ten graph nodes and keeps real-data, credential mutation, deployment, and publication out of scope.

Revision 5 fixes the role vocabulary, release classes, approval-mode mapping, privacy-status v2 target descriptor, closed broker and import contracts, handshake operations, canonical fixture path, exhaustive observation inventory, canonical runner, and proof authority.

The graph is a valid DAG with symmetric parallel edges, repository-prefixed paths, disjoint parallel ownership, explicit region-qualified background.ts handoff, and intent/deliverable/proof for every node.

The test specification crosses the consuming boundaries and includes focused negatives for stale targets, lock/revoke/restart, raw-value disclosure, privacy bypass, unsupported migration, protocol drift, and missing proof keys.
No worker needs to invent a credential, credential path, public API contract, publish identity, or deployment surface before implementation.
rationale: APPROVE. Revision 5 closes the previously blocking contract and privacy-inventory gaps. The exact schemas, operation names, role/mode identifiers, target descriptor, canonical fixture path, observation inventory, synthetic command, evidence directory, and proof-key authority are bound across the brief/spec/plan/test/graph. All ten workers have explicit ownership, dependencies, deliverables, and cheapest proof and can execute without replanning. The remaining items are medium implementation-proof advisories only; none requires inventing a path, credential, API, or publish identity.
nextGate: Proceed to implementation dispatch. Carry R5-A1 through R5-A5 as proof-hardening advisories and preserve the frozen paths, schemas, command, and proof authority.
